newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-START OF MEN'S DOWNHILL DELAYED.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-START OF MEN'S DOWNHILL DELAYED.

text.p: Race organisers on Friday delayed the start of a men's World Cup Alpine skiing downhill by half an hour because of bad weather.
Organisers said the scheduled start of the race, which had been due at 1300 local (1200 GMT), had been moved to 1330 (1230 GMT) with another piste inspection then.
"They must start by two p.m. or they will have to call it off," said one local official. "Frankly, I doubt we'll have a race."
Heavy cloud shrouded the Saslong piste as snow, which began falling in Val Gardena overnight, continued steadily.
Friday's race had already been rescheduled once, after the Canadian resort of Whistler Mountain was unable to stage it earlier this month due to heavy snow.
Race sources in Val Gardena said that if the downhill was unable to be held on Friday it could be staged on Saturday along with another already scheduled for the resort.
In Switzerland, the weather also caused problems for organisers of the women's World Cup when rain and heavy fog prevented a downhill being held in Crans Montana.
